qa_title: Questions homeowners ask about water heaters

qa.q: Should I repair or replace my water heater?
qa.a: A tank that is leaking from the tank itself, or rusted through, can't be patched, so that is a replacement. Problems like a pilot that won't stay lit, a failed thermocouple, a bad control board or a burned-out element are often repairable, which is why the first step is a diagnosis. Age matters too: an older tank is more likely to fail again soon, and the data label on the unit usually shows the manufacture date or a serial number that encodes it. Send a photo of the unit and its data label with your request so the answer starts from the right equipment.

qa.q: What affects the cost of a water heater replacement?
list: The type and size you choose: a standard tank, a power-vent unit, or a tankless conversion.
Fuel: gas or electric, and whether you are keeping it or switching.
Venting: a power-vent or tankless unit may need different venting than the old one.
Where it sits: basement, closet or attic, and how easy it is to get the old unit out and the new one in.
Removal and disposal of the old unit, and any permit the job calls for.
qa.a: No price is listed here because it depends on those points. Ask Shane for a quote. The quickest way is to text photos.

qa.q: How long does a water heater replacement take?
qa.a: A straight swap of a common 40 or 50 gallon gas or electric tank is the quickest job; ask Shane how soon he can do yours. Anything that changes the setup, such as moving the heater, switching fuel or adding venting, takes longer.

qa.q: How often should a water heater be serviced?
qa.a: Follow the manufacturer's instructions for your model. Many call for periodic flushing to clear sediment from the tank. Popping or rumbling noises, rust-colored hot water, or moisture around the base of the tank are signs to have it looked at. If you are weighing a {{boiler-service|boiler with an indirect hot water tank}}, that is a different setup with its own service needs.

send_for_quote: Send with your request: a photo of the water heater and its data label, whether it runs on gas or electric, where it is in the house, and what it is doing (leaking, no hot water, pilot out).

qa.q: Should I repair or replace my boiler?
qa.a: Repair makes sense when one part has failed on a boiler that is otherwise sound: an ignitor, circulator, zone valve, aquastat or low-water cutoff, for example. Replacement is worth discussing when a boiler keeps breaking down, leaks at the boiler body, or is old enough that parts are hard to find. Older boilers also tend to burn more fuel than modern high-efficiency models. Send a photo of the boiler and its data label and describe the symptom or fault code so the quote starts from the right equipment.

qa.q: What is the difference between a cast iron, mod-con and combi boiler?
list: Cast iron: the traditional heavy-section boiler, common in older homes.
Mod-con (modulating condensing): adjusts its output to the demand and recovers extra heat from its exhaust, which needs a condensate drain and plastic venting.
Combi: heats the house and makes domestic hot water from one unit, with no separate tank.
Indirect tank: a separate insulated hot water tank heated by the boiler, so the boiler supplies the hot water too.
qa.a: Which one is right depends on your house, your fuel and your hot water use, so say what you have and what you want when you send your request.

Whether you want an indirect hot water tank with it.

title: Oil to Gas Heating Conversion
seo_title: Oil to Gas Conversion, North Shore & Boston MA | S. Meredith
h1: Oil to gas heating conversion, Saugus to Boston
tagline: Shane's specialty. The boiler, the gas piping, the venting and the permits, explained plainly before you commit.
meta_desc: Oil to gas heating conversion from Saugus to Boston by master plumber Shane Meredith: the steps, cost factors, 2026 rebate rules and answers. 781-820-4592.
intro: Shane is the heat guy, and switching houses from oil to natural gas is his specialty. A conversion is more than a new boiler: gas has to reach the house, a gas line has to run to the equipment, the venting changes, the hot water may change, and the oil tank has to go. This page goes through each part, what changed in 2025 and 2026, and what moves the price, so you can decide with the facts in front of you.

scenarios.b: Whether gas is in front of the house decides the rest of the job. The gas company answers that: National Grid in most of Shane's towns, National Grid or Eversource in Boston and Somerville, and Wakefield Municipal Gas & Light in Wakefield.

Many oil-heated houses north of Boston have a boiler. The usual choices are a high-efficiency gas boiler with an indirect tank for hot water, or a combi boiler that makes heat and hot water in one unit.

Shane runs it himself, from the new gas meter to the boiler, and to a water heater, range or dryer if you want those on gas too. Gas piping is pressure-tested and inspected under a gas permit from your town.

A high-efficiency gas boiler usually vents out the side wall with plastic pipe and does not use the chimney. A gas appliance that does use the chimney may need a liner. The town inspector has the final word.
Many oil boilers also make the hot water through a coil. After the switch, hot water comes from an indirect tank on the new boiler, from a combi boiler, or from a separate water heater.
The old equipment comes out. Removing an oil tank takes a permit from your town fire department.

steps_title: How a conversion goes, step by step

steps.b: A photo of the boiler and its label, the oil tank, and the outside wall where a gas meter could go. Say whether you know if gas is on your street.

steps.h: Confirm gas with the gas company
steps.b: National Grid asks homeowners to fill out its {{https://www.nationalgridus.com/MA-Home/Natural-Gas-Service/Connect-to-Natural-Gas|Natural Gas Availability Form}} and an Electrification Options Acknowledgment Form. It then quotes the service line from your meter location to the gas main, and a main extension if gas is not in front of the house.
Shane goes through a high-efficiency boiler with an indirect tank, or a combi, for your house and the way you use hot water, then gives you a quote for the whole job.
The gas piping is done under a gas permit and checked by the town gas inspector. Removing the oil tank is a separate fire department permit.

The new boiler is piped, vented and wired, the gas piping is pressure-tested, and the gas company sets the meter. Keep the old system working until the new one is ready, so the house is never without heat.
The oil burner and boiler come out, and the tank is removed under the fire department permit.

sections.h: Is converting from oil to gas worth it in 2026?
p: It depends on the house, the age of your equipment and fuel prices, and nobody can honestly promise you a savings figure. Here is what is true this winter:
list: Heating oil in Massachusetts averaged about $6.23 a gallon in late October 2026, about 75% more than a year earlier ({{https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/10/27/metro/high-heating-oil-energy-prices-winter-massachusetts/|Boston Globe}}).

Natural gas rose too: the Massachusetts residential average was $25.77 per thousand cubic feet in January 2026 and $32.10 in August 2026 ({{https://www.eia.gov/dnav/ng/hist/n3010ma3m.htm|U.S. Energy Information Administration}}).
Gas comes by pipe: no deliveries to schedule and no tank to run dry on a cold night.
The usual time to convert is when the oil boiler is old or failing anyway, so you pay for one new heating system instead of repairing the old one first.

p: Gas has to be in the street, or close to it. In Shane's towns the gas company is National Grid almost everywhere; parts of Boston and Somerville are on Eversource, and Wakefield has its own municipal gas company, Wakefield Municipal Gas & Light ({{https://www.mass.gov/info-details/find-my-electric-gas-and-water-company|state list of gas companies by town}}).

Lexington is one of the towns in the state's fossil-free building program, so National Grid asks Lexington customers to check with the town building department before asking for a gas connection. The program is aimed at new construction and major renovations ({{https://www.nationalgridus.com/MA-Home/Natural-Gas-Service/Connect-to-Natural-Gas|National Grid}}).

Connection costs are changing. In August 2025 the state Department of Public Utilities said new gas customers will generally pay the full cost of connecting, ending most free line extensions, once each utility's compliance plan is decided ({{https://commonwealthbeacon.org/energy/massachusetts-signals-new-gas-customers-may-soon-have-to-pay-full-hookup-costs/|CommonWealth Beacon}}). Get the gas company's quote in writing before you sign for the rest of the job.

sections.h: What an oil to gas conversion costs
p: Shane prices each job after seeing the house, so there is no price list here. A national cost guide puts most conversions between $6,000 and $20,000: about $6,000 to $12,000 when a gas line already reaches the house, $12,000 to $20,000 when a new one has to be run, and $1,500 to $4,000 or more for a chimney liner ({{https://homeguide.com/costs/cost-to-convert-from-oil-to-gas|HomeGuide, December 2025}}). What moves the price on a real house:
list: Whether gas is at the street, and what the gas company charges for the service line or main.
The boiler: high-efficiency or standard, combi or boiler with a tank, and its size.
Hot water: an indirect tank, a combi, or a separate water heater.
Venting: a side-wall vent, or a chimney liner.
How far the gas piping runs, and whether the range, dryer or water heater go on gas too.
Heating zones, thermostats and piping changes in the boiler room.
Removing the oil tank, and the permits.

items.t: Mass Save no longer offers rebates, incentives or financing for natural gas, oil or propane heating equipment. Income-eligible households are the exception: they can still get incentives to upgrade existing fossil fuel equipment to high-efficiency models.
The federal Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit (25C) covers improvements made through December 31, 2025, so a boiler installed in 2026 does not qualify.
New gas connections: the state utility regulator (DPU order 20-80-E, August 2025) said new customers will generally pay the full connection cost once utility plans are approved.
National Grid asks for its availability form and an electrification options form before it quotes a service line or main.
items.src: National Grid: Connect to natural gas

items.t: Massachusetts law lets a licensed master or journeyman plumber do gas fitting anywhere in the state, under local permit rules.
Removing an oil tank needs a permit from the local fire department; Saugus has its own application form.
items.src: Town of Saugus tank removal permit (PDF)

guarantee: Master plumber installs, MA license 9630040-PL-M, which covers the gas piping. Gas work is done under your town gas permit and inspection.
qa_title: Questions homeowners ask about switching from oil to gas

qa.q: How long does an oil to gas conversion take?
qa.a: The calendar time depends mostly on the gas company: the availability check, the service line and the meter. The work in the house is shorter; when a customer had no heat, Shane piped and wired a new boiler in one Saturday. Start before the old boiler fails, not during a cold snap.

qa.q: Do I need a new boiler to switch from oil to gas?
qa.a: Usually, yes. An old oil boiler is often near the end of its life, and a new high-efficiency gas boiler burns less fuel than an old one. Send Shane a photo of your boiler and its label and he will tell you what fits your house.

qa.q: Do I need a chimney liner when I switch to gas?
qa.a: It depends on what vents into the chimney. High-efficiency gas boilers vent through the side wall with plastic pipe and do not use the chimney. A gas boiler or water heater that does use the chimney may need a liner, and the town inspector makes the final call. On one of Shane's jobs the homeowner took out an interior chimney altogether, so two power-vent water heaters replaced the two chimney-vented ones.

qa.q: What happens to my oil tank?
qa.a: It is removed under a permit from your town fire department. Ask Shane how the tank is handled on your job when you get your quote.

qa.q: Are there rebates for converting from oil to gas in Massachusetts?
qa.a: Not for most households in 2026. Mass Save stopped rebates, incentives and financing for gas, oil and propane equipment; income-eligible households can still get help upgrading existing equipment. The federal 25C credit covers improvements made through December 31, 2025. Connection terms are changing too, so get the gas company quote in writing.

qa.q: Who do I call first, the gas company or the plumber?
qa.a: Start with the gas company's availability form: it answers whether gas is on your street. National Grid's online application asks for the total gas use of your equipment, so it helps to have your plumber's equipment plan ready when you apply.

qa.q: Combi boiler or a boiler with an indirect tank?
qa.a: A combi makes heat and hot water from one wall-hung unit and saves floor space; it suits smaller homes and moderate hot water use. A boiler with an indirect tank stores hot water, which suits bigger households and several bathrooms. See the {{indirect-water-heaters|indirect water heater page}}.

qa.q: Can Shane do the gas piping too?
qa.a: Yes, Shane does the gas piping himself. In Massachusetts a master plumber license covers gas fitting (chapter 142, section 3), and his is license 9630040-PL-M. Gas piping is pressure-tested and inspected under a gas permit from your town. See {{gas-installation|gas line installation}}.

send_for_quote: Send with your request: photos of the boiler and its label, the oil tank, and the outside wall where a gas meter could go; whether gas is on your street, if you know; how many bathrooms and heating zones you have; and your town.

scenarios.b: Ignition failures, flame sensors and low water pressure trip the safety controls and shut the boiler down. Write down the code on the display before you reset anything.

steps.b: Set to heat and a few degrees above the room temperature. If the screen is blank, change the batteries.
Check the boiler service switch (often at the top of the basement stairs or on the boiler) and the breaker.
Oil: check the tank gauge. Gas: check that the stove or another gas appliance still lights.
Write down any fault code or blinking light. Press reset once; if the boiler locks out again, stop and call.
Note the reading on the boiler gauge. Shane will ask for it.

sections.h: Keep the pipes from freezing while you wait
p: From the {{https://www.redcross.org/get-help/how-to-prepare-for-emergencies/types-of-emergencies/winter-storm/frozen-pipes.html|American Red Cross}} and Shane's own winter tips:
list: Open the cabinet doors under sinks on outside walls so warmer air reaches the pipes.
Let a trickle of cold water run from faucets on outside walls.
Keep the garage door closed if water pipes run through the garage.
Shut off and drain outside faucets, and take the hoses off.
If a pipe has already burst, shut off the main water valve and call.

p: Do not work on the heating if you smell gas. The state's guidance: if you smell gas inside, leave the building and call 911 once you are outside; do not switch lights or appliances on or off ({{https://www.mass.gov/info-details/what-to-do-if-you-smell-gas|Mass.gov: what to do if you smell gas}}).

Gas or oil, and the boiler type if you know it (combi, boiler with a tank).
The fault code or blinking light.
What you already checked.
How long the heat has been off, and whether pipes are at risk.

qa_title: Questions people ask when the heat is out

qa.q: Is no heat an emergency?
qa.a: In freezing weather, yes. Once the house cools, pipes on outside walls can freeze, and a frozen pipe can burst. Shane takes emergency calls 24/7.

qa.q: Should I keep resetting my boiler?
qa.a: No. One reset is reasonable. If the boiler locks out again, the safety control is telling you something is wrong, and repeated resets on an oil burner can let unburned oil build up. Call instead.

qa.q: Why do I have hot water but no heat?
qa.a: On a combi boiler, a stuck diverter valve is a common cause, like the Lynn Navien Shane repaired. On a boiler with an indirect tank, the heating zone circulator or zone valve may have failed while the hot water zone still works. See {{boiler-service|boiler repair}}.

qa.q: Do plumbers fix heating systems?
qa.a: Many do. Shane is a master plumber and heating is his specialty: boilers, combis, indirect tanks, radiators and baseboard, and {{oil-to-gas-conversion|oil to gas conversions}}.

qa.q: What does an emergency heating call cost?
qa.a: Shane does not publish prices; ask when you call. Have the boiler type and the fault code ready so the visit starts with the right parts.

title: Indirect Water Heaters & Combi Hot Water
seo_title: Indirect Water Heater Repair & Replacement | S. Meredith, MA
tagline: Hot water made by your boiler. When the tank leaks, the coil fails or the hot water runs lukewarm, Shane fixes the tank and the boiler zone that feeds it.
meta_desc: Indirect water heater repair and replacement on the North Shore and in Boston: ruptured coils, relief valves, circulators and combi boilers. Call 781-820-4592.
intro: An indirect water heater is an insulated tank heated by your boiler through a coil, so the boiler makes your hot water too. When the hot water goes lukewarm, the tank leaks or the boiler relief valve starts dripping, the cause can be the tank or the boiler zone that heats it. Shane works on both sides: he replaced an 80-gallon indirect tank whose ruptured coil was pushing house water pressure into the boiler, and a burned-out circulator on another home's indirect zone.

scenarios.b: House water leaks into the boiler loop, the boiler pressure climbs and the relief valve discharges. The fix is a new tank.
The tank is fine but the boiler stops sending heat to it. A drip from a purge valve burned out one customer's circulator.
A tank leaking at the bottom or at its fittings needs to be replaced.
A combi makes hot water on demand with no tank. A stuck diverter valve can leave you with hot water but no heat, as on a Lynn Navien Shane repaired.

scenarios.h: A new indirect with a new boiler
scenarios.b: Paired with a high-efficiency boiler, like the Haverhill install with five heating zones.

qa_title: Questions homeowners ask about indirect water heaters

qa.q: Why is my indirect water heater not making hot water?
qa.a: Usually the boiler is not heating it: a failed circulator or zone valve, a control setting, or the boiler itself is down. If your heat works but the hot water does not, the problem is likely on the tank zone.

qa.q: Why is my boiler relief valve dripping?
qa.a: One cause is a ruptured coil in an indirect tank letting house water pressure into the boiler, which is what Shane found before the 80-gallon replacement. A failed expansion tank or fill valve can do it too. A dripping relief valve is a warning: call.

qa.q: Indirect water heater or a regular water heater?
qa.a: A regular (direct) water heater has its own burner or elements. An indirect has none; the boiler heats it. Indirects suit homes that already run a boiler. For regular tanks, see {{water-heater-replacement|water heater repair and replacement}}.

qa.q: What does an indirect water heater replacement cost?

intro: When one room stays cold, or the baseboard is warm at one end and cold at the other, the problem is usually in the piping between the boiler and the radiators: air in the loop, a stuck zone valve, a failed circulator or a leak. qa.q: Why is my radiator not heating up?
qa.a: Common causes are air trapped at the top, a closed or stuck valve, a zone valve that does not open, or a circulator that has stopped. If a radiator stays cold after bleeding, the problem is elsewhere in the loop.

qa.q: Why is only one room cold?
qa.a: Usually one zone or one radiator is the problem: a zone valve, its thermostat, air in that run, or a blocked pipe. If the whole house is cold, see {{no-heat-emergency|no heat}}.

qa.q: Can you add heat to a finished basement?
qa.a: Yes, by adding a heating zone off the boiler when the boiler has the capacity for it. Shane checks the boiler and plans the piping before quoting.

qa.q: Should I fix a small drip on my heating pipes?
qa.a: Yes, before the cold weather. A steady drip lowers the boiler pressure, and on one of Shane's jobs a drip from a purge valve led to a burned-out circulator and a cold shower.
